title: Salsiccia e Fagioli
subtitle: Italian pork sausages braised with cannellini beans
excerpt: Coarse Italian pork sausages cooked with cannellini beans, tomatoes, and rosemary in one pot. The beans absorb the fat from the sausages and the sauce thickens into something deeply savoury. Good bread alongside is not optional.
sourceNotes: Tuscan cucina povera tradition. Synthesised from classic fagioli all'uccelletto with the addition of sausage.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely and freeze in portions. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a wider pan so the sausages brown without steaming.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day. Reheat slowly on the hob, adding water if needed.

content.text: This is a one-pan braise that needs very little attention. Brown the sausages well before adding anything else. That colour is where the flavour lives.
Heat the olive oil in the large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the sausages and brown on all sides for about 8 minutes. Set them aside on a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the garlic and rosemary to the pan fat. Cook for 1 minute until the garlic is pale gold.
Add the chilli flakes if using. Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Stir and bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cannellini beans and nestle the sausages back in. Season with salt and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes. The sauce should thicken and coat the beans. If it looks dry, add a splash of water.
Rest for 5 minutes. Discard the rosemary sprigs. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil and serve with bread.

items.symptom: The sauce is too thin after 20 minutes.
items.cause: Too much liquid was added or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Increase the heat and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes more, stirring occasionally.

items.symptom: The sausages burst and break apart.
items.cause: They were not pricked before cooking and the heat was too high.
items.fix: Prick sausages well before browning and keep the heat at medium, not high.

items.symptom: The beans are turning to mush.
items.cause: They were added too early or simmered at a hard boil.
items.fix: Add beans later in the cook and keep the heat at a gentle simmer.
